normalized.governing_thought: Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon, reject the 600-door retail launch, and hold Japan for later
executive_summary: The opportunity is real and it is on Amazon.

US K-beauty facial skincare reached $3.6B in 2025, growing 17% a year against 5% for the category; 41% of it sells on Amazon. Onsoo's cross-border pilot was running at about $4M a year by June 2026 on three SKUs, rated 4.5 stars.
Amazon-led (A) is the only US route that passes the board's cash and margin tests.
On planning inputs, A needs at most $1.9M of cash (the cap is $18M), pays back in 2030 (+$2.4M cumulative) and keeps group margin above 9% every year.
Retail-led (B) fails on its own numbers, and its inputs are optimistic.

Cumulative cash reaches –$18.9M in 2029 and –$20.8M in 2030 with no payback; group margin falls to 4.5% in 2027. At Onsoo's under-10% awareness, newcomers sell 2.6 units per door per week, not the 4.5 assumed and below the 4.0 delisting line. Corrected, B needs about $26M of cash.
A's payback is fragile, but its downside is small.

Payback by 2030 needs advertising cost of sales (ACoS) at or below 28.6% (plan 25%, pilot 28%, median brand at this scale 32%) and volumes near plan (at 80% of plan it only just pays back). At 32% ACoS A misses payback (–$2.3M at end-2030), but the worst combined case we modelled peaks at $4.6M and the margin floor always holds.

A reaches $26M in 2030. B's $38M rests on the inflated inputs; corrected it is about $28M. $40M should be the goal of a gated second phase in specialty retail, which comes back to the board as its own investment case.

Decisions requested in March 2027: (1) approve Option A as Onsoo's single 2027 launch; (2) approve a US cash envelope of $5M through 2030, enough for 80% of plan volume with 32% ACoS and a 25% duty (–$4.6M peak), with anything beyond returning to the board; (3) decline the 600-door retail launch; (4) adopt tighter gates for specialty retail, including aided awareness above 20%, not 15%; (5) re-base the plan at 30–32% ACoS rather than 25%.

slides.title: How we built the numbers, and the choices we made where the pack was silent

claims.claim: Method
evidence: All inputs are the planning team's, as given in the briefing pack; no outside data is used.
Per-unit economics of the hero product (Rice Ferment Barrier Cream) are applied to all SKUs, as the planning team does.
Cash = operating profit minus the change in inventory, which is held at four months of landed cost. No tax, receivables or payables.
Group margin adds each option's operating profit and revenue to the ex-US plan (revenue $140–158M at an 11.0% margin).
ACoS breakeven: the ACoS at which A's cumulative cash is exactly zero at end-2030, holding plan volumes.
Exchange rate held at KRW 1,380 per dollar; a weaker won would lower dollar product costs.

claims.claim: Judgement calls
evidence: Ambition read as $40M of US revenue in 2030 (Onsoo's own revenue, with retail at wholesale).
2027 volumes treated as full-year, as in the planning team's tables.
One-time costs and door fixtures expensed in the year incurred (this makes the margin test conservative).
Onsoo placed in the "below 10%" awareness band (4% of all buyers, 9% of K-beauty buyers).
The bandwidth limit read as applying to 2027 only, so a Japan scale-up can be considered for 2028.
Proposed trigger levels and the $5M cash envelope are our recommendations, not board-set figures.
Japan figures used as given (the pack has no Japan working capital).

claims.claim: Choices marked here were made without the CEO's input and should be confirmed before the board meeting.

normalized.recommendation: Launch Amazon-led in 2027, scale in 2028, and open specialty retail only when the evidence clears tighter gates. Approve Option A, Amazon-led US entry in 2027, as Onsoo's single major launch for the year; approve a cumulative US cash envelope of $5M through 2030, reported quarterly against the guardrails; decline the 600-door national specialty-retail launch in 2027; adopt four retail gates (Amazon above $10M, aided awareness above 20%, a door test at 4.0 or more units per week, and a retail loss that fits within the 8% margin floor); direct the planning team to re-base Option A at 30–32% ACoS and bring a 2028 Japan scale-up case to the board in late 2027.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Chosen. The only US route that passes the board's cash and margin tests; peak cash $1.9M, pays back in 2030 (+$2.4M), lowest group margin 9.5%. At risk on ambition ($26.4M in 2030) and payback (needs ACoS ≤ 28.6% and volume near plan).

alternatives_considered.option: B · Retail-led national specialty-retail launch in 600 doors (advocate: independent board member)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected/declined: it breaches the cap, misses payback and breaks the margin floor even on its own inputs (–$20.8M cumulative cash by 2030, group margin 4.5% in 2027). Its inputs are optimistic (2.6 units per door per week at Onsoo's awareness vs 4.5 assumed; halo not causal); corrected it needs about $26M of cash for ~$28M revenue.

alternatives_considered.option: J · Japan scale-up (advocate: Head of Japan)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Not chosen for 2027: the safe option but a small one ($7M revenue by 2030 in a market growing 1.5% a year) and builds no US business. Lower-risk and beats A on cash at 32% ACoS. Held for later: can return as a 2028 decision; planning team to bring a 2028 Japan scale-up case in late 2027.

alternatives_considered.option: CEO's plan: add specialty retail from 2029 once Amazon passes $10M and awareness passes 15%
alternatives_considered.treatment: Modified: retail returns as a separate investment case only if four tighter gates clear, including aided awareness above 20% (not 15%); B's $7.5M programme added in 2029 would cut group margin to 6.3% and take cash to –$11.8M.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Built only from the planning team's briefing pack (synthetic data); no outside data is used.
All figures in US dollars at KRW 1,380 per dollar; a weaker won would lower dollar product costs.
A's payback is fragile: needs ACoS at or below 28.6% (26.9% with a 25% duty) and volumes near plan; the plan's 25% ACoS runs against the evidence (pilot 28%, benchmark median 32%).
Volume plan is a stretch: 2027 is 1.8× the June pilot run-rate and pilot growth slowed to ~9% a month; at 80% of plan A only just pays back, at 70% it misses.
US duty on Korean cosmetics decision due mid-2027 (15% plan; 25% case); tariff cases apply 25% from 2027 so are slightly conservative.
Ambition read as $40M of US revenue in 2030; on a looser "trajectory" reading, A and B would be closer to passing.
Per-unit economics of the hero product (Rice Ferment Barrier Cream) are applied to all SKUs.
Cash = operating profit minus change in inventory (four months of landed cost); no tax, receivables or payables.
One-time costs and door fixtures expensed in the year incurred (makes the margin test conservative).
Onsoo placed in the "below 10%" awareness band.
Bandwidth limit read as applying to 2027 only.
"B corrected" is illustrative only as it assumes retail is kept running.
Japan figures used as given (the pack has no Japan working capital).
Proposed trigger levels and the $5M cash envelope are recommendations, not board-set figures; trigger levels are for management to confirm.
Choices were made without the CEO's input and should be confirmed before the board meeting.
Amazon-first is no guarantee: of three K-beauty brands that entered Amazon-first, one reached ~$30M by 2025; two stayed below $5M.
